method: Read all 21 outgoing and 12 incoming primary bodies in full from voyage.packet.json in bounded batches, recording every retained body paragraph, then compared the texts with initial_survey.json and checked proposed quote substrings against the packet.

findings: The 105/106 offer bundle is two distinct incoming communications: 105 is Henslow's recommendation and 106 is Peacock's offer. Darwin's 107 distinguishes Peacock's arrival and personal receipt; 121 later uses the plural 'letters from Peacock & Henslow'.

DCP-LETT-116 is a plausible identified source for the letter Darwin says he received from Sedgwick in 123, but 123 explicitly says it was unread, so no geological content from 116 is knowledge available in 123.

DCP-LETT-135 supports DCP-LETT-139 through the distinctive shoregoing-fellows phrase. It does not support DCP-LETT-142, whose acknowledged FitzRoy input contains baggage-by-another-vessel and talc details absent from 135.
DCP-LETT-125 to DCP-LETT-135A is a supported direct correspondence link; 135A separately reports receipt of fungi, which is not letter evidence.
DCP-LETT-143 to DCP-LETT-144 is supported by matching consignment directions and accounting discussion.
The Ramsay memorial source answered in 152 is unlocated. Editorial identification or thematic similarity cannot turn 150 into that source.
DCP-LETT-139 retains the XML 4-or-11 October alternatives; its weekday does not resolve them.
limitations: This review is limited to the 21 outgoing and 12 incoming bodies in voyage.packet.json. Missing letters, third-party Wood/FitzRoy communications, oral meetings, parcels and newspapers remain separate evidence classes.
